The payout curve generator models trust and engagement dynamics as a stochastic process governed by bounded risk. It assumes that higher trust correlates with lower financial risk, and that payout curves must remain invertible under trust thresholds. The legal boundary validator enforces binary compliance states, ensuring no real-money flows occur without approval. The data isolation layer ensures all inputs are either synthetic or consented, preventing leakage. These primitives form a dual constraint system: one probabilistic (trust-engagement) and one deterministic (legal/data). Failure modes include trust collapse, unauthorized real-money flow, and data breach. The system is robust under these dualities but fails when assumptions about trust or consent are violated.
